# Load in libraries and data
```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
library(base)
library(readxl)
library(DESeq2)
library(pheatmap)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(ggplot2)
library(magrittr)
library(GSVA)
library(msigdbr)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(Glimma)
library(PCAtools)
library(clusterProfiler)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)
})

#Read in bulk RNA sequencign counts and metadata files
#organoid counts is the combined filtered_count_matrix_organoid_samples.txt
organoids_counts <- read.table("geo_upload_files/filtered_count_matrix_organoid_samples.txt", header = T, quote = "", sep = "\t")
metadata <- read.csv("metadata_coculture_organoids.csv") 


```

# DESeq2 Analyss
```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#create our deseq2 dataset combining metadata that shows tissue type and patient ID with the sample ID from sequencing information
#corrected for batch and including all of the metadata we read in. 
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = organoids_counts,
                              colData = metadata,
                              design = ~ batch)

#differntial expression analysis
dds <- DESeq(dds)
resultsNames(dds)
res <- results(dds)
res

#DESeq(): Normalizes counts, estimates fold changes, runs main DESeq2 pipeline.
#resultsNames(): Shows available coefficients from the model (e.g., batch vs batch2, condition vs control, etc.).
#results(dds): Extracts results table (DE genes: logFC, p-values, etc.).
vst <- assay(vst(dds))
#vst(dds): Applies DESeq2’s variance stabilizing transformation to your counts. 
#This makes the data more homoscedastic (variance less dependent on mean)—crucial for PCA 
#and plotting.
#assay(...): Extracts just the transformed count matrix.

rv <- rowVars(vst)
select <- order(rv, decreasing=TRUE)[seq_len(min(500, length(dds)))]

#rowVars(vst): For each gene, compute variance across all samples. 
#Genes with higher variance are more informative for PCA (they drive sample differences).
#order(rv, decreasing=TRUE): Ranks genes from most to least variable.
#select ...: Picks the top 500 variable genes—or, if you have fewer than 500 genes, 
#just all of them. This is a classic way to focus PCA on the key “drivers” of sample separation.
pca <- pca(vst[select,], metadata = colData(dds))
biplot(pca,
       showLoadings = F,
       boxedLoadingsNames = T,
       colby = 'patient_id',
       shape = 'tissue',
       labSize = 0, pointSize = 5,
       legendPosition = 'right',
       legendLabSize = 7, legendIconSize = 4, legendTitleSize = 10)

#Differentially expressed genes
# ── Differential Expression: Cell Line 1594 vs 1253 ──────────────────────────

# 1. Set cell line as a factor with 1253 as reference, directly on existing dds
dds$patient_id <- factor(dds$patient_id, levels = c("1253", "1594"))

# 2. Update the design to control for batch and test cell line effect
design(dds) <- ~ patient_id

# 3. Run DESeq2
dds <- DESeq(dds)
resultsNames(dds)  # Should show "patient_id_1594_vs_1253"

# 4. Extract results
res_cl <- results(dds,
                  name  = "patient_id_1594_vs_1253",
                  alpha = 0.05)
summary(res_cl)

# 5. Shrink LFC estimates
res_cl_shrunk <- lfcShrink(dds,
                           coef = "patient_id_1594_vs_1253",
                           type = "ashr")

# 6. Export to data frame
res_df <- as.data.frame(res_cl_shrunk) %>%
  rownames_to_column("ensembl_id") %>%
  arrange(padj)

gene_symbols <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db,
                                      keys    = rownames(dds),
                                      columns = c("ENSEMBL", "SYMBOL"),
                                      keytype = "ENSEMBL") %>%
  distinct(ENSEMBL, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  column_to_rownames("ENSEMBL")

rownames(res_df) <- res_df[,1]

head(rownames(res_df))
head(rownames(gene_symbols))


res_df <- res_df %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  merge(gene_symbols, by = 0) %>%
  filter(!is.na(padj)) %>%
  rename(gene_id = Row.names) %>%
  mutate(status = ifelse(log2FoldChange > 0.5 & padj < 0.05, 1,
                         ifelse(log2FoldChange < -0.5 & padj < 0.05, -1, 0))) %>%
  arrange(padj)


head(res_df, 20)

write.csv(res_df, "DE_1594_vs_1253.csv", row.names = FALSE)


#you will collapse the technical replicates to make sure the analysis is being performed on
#biologically active samples; it is also critical that you sum them and not average as that is standard in the field
#DDS is the raw master data used for differential gene expression
#VST is variance stabilized and is used for PCA, clustering, heatmaps etc.
#VST controls for how skewed this data is. 
dds <- collapseReplicates(dds, dds$patient_id)
vst <- assay(vst(dds))
rv <- rowVars(vst)
select <- order(rv, decreasing=TRUE)[seq_len(min(500, length(dds)))]
pca <- pca(vst[select,], metadata = colData(dds))
biplot(pca,
       showLoadings = F,
       boxedLoadingsNames = T,
       colby = 'patient_id',
       shape = 'tissue',
       labSize = 0, pointSize = 5, 
       legendPosition = 'right',
       legendLabSize = 7, legendIconSize = 4, legendTitleSize = 10)


#Heat map
# Combine all your genes of interest

library(RColorBrewer)
genes_of_interest <- c("ADAM10", "FGFR2", "GAS5",
                       "FZD5", "RYK", "SEMA3A",
                       "VEGFA", "SEMA3B", "NRP1",
                       "ROR1", "SEMA3C", "VEGFB",
                       "RERG", "IL32", "IFITM2", "ROR2",
                       "NRG4", "MMP3", "TGFB2", "IL7",
                       "NRG1", "MMP12")


gene_map <- gene_symbols[gene_symbols$SYMBOL %in% genes_of_interest, , drop = FALSE]
selected_genes <- vst[rownames(gene_map), , drop = FALSE]
head(rownames(gene_map))
head(rownames(vst))
sum(rownames(gene_map) %in% rownames(vst))

df <- as.data.frame(colData(dds))

pheatmap(selected_genes, scale = 'none', cluster_rows = TRUE, show_rownames = TRUE, show_colnames = TRUE,
         cluster_cols = FALSE, border_color = "black", cellwidth = 10, cellheight = 10,
         labels_row = gene_map$SYMBOL[match(rownames(selected_genes), rownames(gene_map))],
         col = colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(9, "RdBu")))(15))




```
